title: I'm Wearing It: Definite viselem vs. Indefinite viselek

sections.content: Hungarian verbs have two present-tense conjugations. The indefinite form (viselek) is used with no object, or an unspecified one. The definite form (viselem) is used when the object is a specific, known thing -- often marked by ez/az or 'the'.
Because ezt ('this one') is a specific, already-identified object, the verb must switch to the definite form viselem, not viselek. This same switch happens with many verbs, e.g. szeretek vs szeretem.
